headline: Congress cancels a 2024 federal decision that limited oil and gas leasing in Alaska's Arctic National Wildlife Refuge coastal plain.
what_it_does: This law cancels a December 2024 Bureau of Land Management decision about oil and gas leasing in the Coastal Plain area of the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge. That 2024 decision had closed about 1.2 million of the area's roughly 1.6 million acres to oil and gas leasing and exploration, leaving only the legal minimum of 400,000 acres open. With the 2024 decision undone, more of the coastal plain can be opened for oil and gas leasing, as it was under an earlier 2020 decision. Under the Congressional Review Act, the agency generally cannot issue a substantially similar rule again unless Congress allows it.

who_it_affects.how: They may be able to bid on leases across more of the roughly 1.6 million acres of the coastal plain instead of only about 400,000 acres.
The agency can no longer use its 2024 decision to manage leasing in the coastal plain and generally cannot issue a substantially similar rule.

who_it_affects.group: Alaska residents and communities near the refuge
who_it_affects.how: About 1.2 million acres that the 2024 decision had set aside to protect resources and certain uses could now be open to oil and gas leasing.
